_owner: wizard — written by `togo builder new`. No agent may write this file (Rule 38).
_purpose: The data the guard hooks read instead of hard-coding project facts.
The ancestor estate's guards embedded product binary names, GKE pod names, Terraform module paths and
database hostnames directly in the shell source, which meant every new product forked the
hook. Here the hook source is generic and this file is the only thing that changes.
Consumed by: session-init.sh · guard-db-wipe.sh · guard-db-dml.sh · guard-direct-ddl.sh ·
CONTRACT: a hook that cannot parse this file EXITS 0. A guard never blocks on its own bug.

binaries._note: Product binaries whose destructive subcommands the guards police. `guard-db-wipe.sh` blocks `<binary> <destructive_subcommand>` against any non-ephemeral target. the ancestor estate hard-coded its own product binaries here; this is that list, parameterized.
binaries._destructive_note: `<binary> reset` is the exact command that dropped the public schema in the 2026-06-21 platform-wide wipe. It is blocked outright unless the target is explicitly ephemeral.

migration_runner._note: THE sanctioned path. Commands matching these patterns pass every DDL/DML guard — they are how schema and data changes are supposed to happen. Everything else that touches a database is blocked.
migration_runner._queries_note: db/queries/** is the ONLY place SQL may be hand-written (Rule 13). togo IS sqlc + Atlas + an ORM; hand-written SQL anywhere else is banned.

protected_databases._note: Names, hosts and URL fragments that identify a REAL database. Any destructive operation matching one of these is blocked unconditionally — no override flag, no `--force`, no 'I checked, it's fine'. Add every shared environment here, including the ones you think nobody uses.

ephemeral_targets._note: The ONLY places a destructive operation may run. A command must EXPLICITLY name one of these to be let through — an unqualified `psql -c 'TRUNCATE ...'` is blocked, because 'it was pointed at local' is not a claim a guard can verify after the fact.

runtime_ddl._note: Rule 20's togo-specific clause, and the violation this framework is most likely to produce. In a plugin architecture where every plugin self-registers via init() and could self-migrate on boot, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` from service code is a one-line habit that silently makes the migration history a lie. togo's own auth and autopilot plugins both do it today. guard-direct-ddl.sh scans Go source for these patterns.

auto_migrate_env_vars._note: Setting any of these true via a deploy re-arms a destructive boot-time migration. Blocked by guard-db-wipe.sh AND by Rule 26 (a deploy never sets configuration).

generated_files._note: Rule 11 / guard-generated-files.sh. Hand-editing a generated file is the cheapest togo violation to make and the cheapest to catch: the next `togo generate` silently reverts it, and the bug comes back a week later with no trace of why.

sources_of_truth.web/src/**/*.gen.ts: the OpenAPI export produced by `togo generate`

secrets._note: Rule 34 / guard-secrets.sh. Paths whose CONTENT must never be read, printed, echoed, committed or relocated, plus the shapes that must be dropped from any output before it leaves the process.
secrets.rotation: human-only — an exposed secret is rotated by the operator, never 'cleaned up' by an agent

git._note: Rule 42 / guard-scoped-add.sh. The ancestor estate recorded 'never git add -A' as a bare NEVER with no enforcement; here it is a block. An unscoped add is how a run's .env, its scratch files and its half-finished second idea end up in the commit that gets reviewed.

deploy._note: Rule 25/26/27. `guard-autonomy.sh` treats every command here as a must_ask. `session-init.sh` prints the target for the current branch.

forbidden_on_deploy._note: Rule 26 — a deploy never sets configuration. Config has exactly one source of truth and the deploy command is not it.

iac._note: Nullable — null when project.json.iac is null, in which case Rules 24/25 are not shipped and these checks are inert. When non-null, guard-db-wipe.sh additionally refuses an apply while a DB StatefulSet in one of these modules carries container args (the 2026-06-22 pod-restart-into-initdb wipe path).

session._note: What session-init.sh prints. The autonomy line is the single most useful thing an operator can see at session start — it is what tells them, before they type anything, how much this session may do on its own.

budget._note: Mirrors autonomy.yaml.budget so budget-meter.sh can read one file. autonomy.yaml is authoritative; the wizard keeps these in sync and `togo builder doctor --claude` asserts they match.
